description:
Three days before Thanksgiving, Grandma Inez gives Mia a whistle and one job: nobody touches the pie. Every snacker she catches has to catch the next one, and the oven timer has seen everything.

lines.text: Mia, raise your right hand. As of today, you are the Kitchen Patrol.
Yes, Grandma. What are the rules?
Three days to Thanksgiving. Nobody touches the pie. Nobody touches the stuffing. Nobody touches anything.
What if somebody touches something?
Then you point, you blow that whistle, and you say the words.
You're under arrest!
Lovely. I have been on this counter for nine years. Finally, some law and order.
Who said that?
The oven timer, madam. I only count. I do not judge. Mostly.
Ignore the timer. He beeps when he's nervous. Patrol starts now.
Good morning, ladies. Just walking by. Just a man, walking, near some marshmallows.
Uncle Terrence. Why is there a marshmallow in your mustache?
That is not a marshmallow. That is a very small cloud. It's weather.
It has been in there for forty seconds. I counted.
You're under arrest!
On what charge?
Sweet potato topping. First degree.
I want a lawyer. Or a cracker. Whatever is closer.
Rules are rules, Terrence. Now you're on patrol too. That's how it works.
Wait, so if I get arrested, I get a badge?
Everybody you catch has to catch somebody else.
Oh, this is a pyramid scheme. I love it.
Timer. You beeped at six this morning and woke up the entire house.
The rolls were done, sir. I am a professional.
There were no rolls. You beeped at an empty oven.
I was practicing. Thursday is a big day for me.
You're under arrest!
Fine. But I have no hands. You will have to carry me to jail. Mind the cord.
Grandma, where is jail?
The jail is the kids' table. Everybody hates it there.
I'm forty six. I'm not sitting at the kids' table.
You put a marshmallow in your face, baby. You made your choice.
My turn. I have seen things on this counter. Terrible things.
Like what?
Every night at midnight, somebody eats one bite of crust off the edge of the pie. Then turns the pie around.
The pie gets smaller every day. I thought it was shy.
Somebody is turning the pie so we don't see the bite!
Seven nights. Seven bites. A very round crime.
Who is it? I need a name!
I am a timer, madam. I do not see faces. I only hear slippers. Fuzzy ones.
Everybody here wears fuzzy slippers.
Then everybody take off your slippers. Right now.
Well. Would you look at the time. I should go check on the yams.
Grandma. Your slippers have crumbs on them.
Those are decorative crumbs. They came with the slippers.
Also, there is a pie tin in her purse. It says store bought. Aisle nine.
Store bought? Mama, your famous homemade pie?
I have made that pie from scratch for thirty years. The scratch is aisle nine.
You made me the patrol so nobody would check your purse!
I made you the patrol because you're seven and you love a whistle. The purse was a bonus.
Thirty years. I told my wife your crust was a family secret.
It is a secret. It's a family secret now. Nobody tells your aunties.
I have known since two thousand ten. Nobody asks the timer anything.
Grandma Inez. You're under arrest.
Fine. But the jail is the kids' table, and I'm bringing the pie.
Wait, if she's in jail, who's cooking Thanksgiving?
The Kitchen Patrol. Congratulations, baby. You're the chef now.
I'm seven! I can only make cereal!
Cereal Thanksgiving. I would eat that every year.
Excellent. I will start counting. Do not beep at me.
Uncle Terrence. Why is there a pie crust in your mustache?
That is weather.
